update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency sports stadiums in India and globally, focusing on location matching and capacity extremes for Sports Static GK.

largest_stadiums_by_category.key_fact: The largest cricket stadium and the largest overall stadium in the world by capacity (132,000). Formerly known as Motera Stadium.
Recognized by Guinness World Records as the largest fully-seated hockey arena in the world (capacity ~21,800). Built for the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup.

largest_stadiums_by_category.stadium_name: Salt Lake Stadium (Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan)
largest_stadiums_by_category.key_fact: The largest football stadium in India by seating capacity (approx. 85,000).
India's first and only motor racing circuit capable of hosting Formula One (hosted the Indian Grand Prix from 2011 to 2013).

famous_cricket_stadiums_india.key_fact: Established in 1864, it is the oldest and second-largest cricket stadium in India. Often called the 'Mecca of Indian cricket'.
Headquarters of the BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India). Famous for hosting the 2011 Cricket World Cup Final where India won.
Formerly known as Feroz Shah Kotla Stadium. The second oldest functional international cricket stadium in India.
The first cricket stadium in the world to use solar panels to generate a bulk of the electricity needed to run the stadium.
Established in 1916, making it the oldest continuously used cricket stadium in India.
One of the few international cricket stadiums in India not owned by the state cricket association (owned by the Sports Department of UP).
An iconic venue that frequently hosts both cricket and football matches.
Built during the reign of Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II.

other_prominent_stadiums_india.key_fact: Served as the venue for the first Asian Games in 1951.
Co-hosted the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup along with the Birsa Munda Stadium.
The main stadium for the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

iconic_international_stadiums.key_fact: Widely known as the 'Home of Cricket'. Owned by the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).
The second-largest cricket stadium in the world and the largest in the Southern Hemisphere.
Famous for its red clay courts. It is the premier venue for the French Open Grand Slam tournament.
The main court at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club, famous for hosting the Wimbledon Championships on grass.
